answer: In a market where agents buy dawn surveys of a reef and its rocky ledge, the broker requires each agent identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before receiving a daily quota of requests. Creating more keys does not bypass the bond: every extra quota requires another deposit. A swarm of 10,000 fake agents therefore ties up $1 million for a month, imposing a capital cost even if the attacker later recovers every bond.
